separable_target_sentences.target_qualitative_prior_art: In common with the initial published report of ASPS-[number masked], results also confirmed expression of GPNMB (Kenney et al., [number masked]).

Over-expressed transcripts found in the nearest cluster group and ASPS-[number masked] included GPNMB, CRYAB, FABP3, and CTSK, which are markers of mesenchymal cells (Debnath et al., [number masked]; Kulterer et al., [number masked]; Wang Jr et al, [number masked]; Yu et al., [number masked]).

As could be anticipated, GPNMB was the highest expressed mRNA; followed by novel surface makers such as the glutamate transporter SLC3[number masked]A1 and the amyloid beta (A4) precursor protein APP.

Meta-analysis of data from these four in vivo studies had considerable overlap, emphasizing the consistent upregulation of mRNAs such as GPNMB, ABCB5, PSG9, CYP1[number masked]A1, PRL, SULT1C2, and SV2B.
Glycoprotein Nmb (GPNMB) should be recognized as the prototypic cell surface marker for ASPS.
As stated, GPNMB is recognized as a marker of mesenchymal cells (Kuci et al., [number masked]).

Interestingly, within protein atlas, the cell line designated ‘ASC diff’, a differentiated adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell line has the highest expression of GPNMB and also expresses TRIM6[number masked], CRYAB, FABP3, and CTSK.
